label: Woodland floor
summary: The floor under closed stands of trees on the deep rough near play: heath on dry knolls, bilberry under conifers, herbs under broadleaves and ferns in wet hollows, with brush along a stand's rim and in drifts inside the forest.
steps: Reads Unity's surface map of the built course (golfmap.surfaces.export), the terrain's DEM next to it and the planted trees (<prefix>-<terrain>-trees.json); without planted trees it writes no floor.

Each tree's crown is a disc on the ground (at least min-crown wide), conifer or broadleaf; a tree species area whose mix is all conifers (conifer-species) or all broadleaves sets the kind of the stems inside it.

Grows only on deep rough, never on a rock slab, within reach of play, with the tall rough's clearances from tees, greens, fairways, bunkers, water and houses (the tall-grass rules), and it does not spill into the mown rough.

It also takes the tall rough's default thinning far from play (far-start, far-ramp, far-weight in tall-grass.json: 0.56 beyond 40 m) - the code default, not the course's own tall-grass values, which reach only the tall rough.
The floor comes in where the crowns, smoothed over closure-smooth, close past floor-closure: a lone tree or a loose row keeps the tall rough under it, a gap in a stand opens the floor.
From the DEM it works out the slope, the terrain position (height above the mean ground within tpi-radius) and a wetness index (where water gathers and stays).

Which floor (woodland_floor/fern, heath, bilberry, herb): wet ground that is not a slope is fern; a knoll is heath, mostly under conifers; level ground is bilberry under conifers and herb under broadleaves, by the conifer share of the crowns around a point.

Each floor's score gets its own smooth noise so patches have ragged borders, and two floors cross-fade over type-blend; it picks again in small pockets where the noise counts for more, so a bilberry floor holds pockets of fern, heather or grass.
Along a stand's rim towards open ground it plants woodland_floor/edge (bushes and saplings), a mix layer over whatever floor or tall rough is there; a lone tree's own rim gets none.
Inside what is decidedly forest, not a tree corridor between two holes, it plants woodland_floor/brush (saplings and bushes) in drifts, a mix layer too.
Written like the tall rough: nested weight bands, one zone per band polygon, with paths and roads cut out; the floors first, then the edge and brush layers.

rules.text: No floor further than this from play (rough, semi, fairway, green, tee, bunker).
Over the last metres before reach the floor fades out instead of stopping.
How far the floor reaches from the deep rough into the mown rough (none).
A tree's crown on the ground is at least a disc this wide (radius).
The crowns are smoothed over this (sigma) to give the canopy closure.
No floor below the first closure, full floor above the second: a lone tree keeps the tall rough under it.
A tree species area whose species all contain one of these makes its stems conifers; none of them, broadleaves.
The conifer share is that of the stand around a point (crowns smoothed over this), not of the one tree over it.
Fern ground: not wet below the first wetness, fully wet above the second (Vreta's woodland: 4.3 .. 11).
Water does not stay on a slope: wet ground counts fully below the first slope and not at all above the second.
Heath ground: not a knoll below this height above the ground around it, fully one above the second (Vreta's woodland: -1.3 .. 1.1).
Heath's score on a knoll under broadleaves, against 1 under conifers (a broadleaf knoll is a dry herb slope as often as heath).
Bilberry's score on a conifer knoll (1 on level conifer ground).
Herb's score on a broadleaf knoll (1 on level broadleaf ground).
How far each floor's noise moves its score, so the patches have ragged borders.
Size of the noise blobs, so of the floor patches.
Two floors cross-fade over this (sigma) instead of meeting on a line; pockets over half of it.
Size of the pockets of another floor inside a patch.
How much the score still counts when the pockets are picked (the noise counts 1).
Share of the floor's weight that goes to the pockets.
Slope, terrain position and wetness are worked out on cells this size (a 0.5 m lidar grid is noise at the scale plants answer to).
The terrain position is the height above the mean ground within this radius.
The wetness index is smoothed over this (sigma): a wet strip, not a one-cell thread down the flow line.
Flatter ground counts as this steep for the wetness index (dead flat ground would be endlessly wet).
The rim of a stand (woodland_floor/edge): none below the first closure, full at the second, none again above the third.
A rim belongs to a stand: the crowns smoothed over this (sigma) ...
... must close this far (no edge below the first, full above the second), so a lone tree's own rim gets no brush.
Decidedly forest (woodland_floor/brush): the crowns smoothed over this (sigma) ...
... close this far, which a tree corridor between two holes does not (Vreta's floor: median 0.31).
The brush stands in drifts of about this size ...
... where its noise passes these levels (none below the first, full above the second: about two thirds of the forest).
The zone type of the zones (variants heath, bilberry, herb, fern, edge, brush).
The contour levels the weight field is written at (one zone per band; the top band has weight 1).
Feather of each weight band.
Outlines are simplified to this tolerance.
Band pieces smaller than this are dropped (also after the paths and roads are cut out).
